cards.text: One Sabbath, Jesus is passing through the grainfields with His disciples. As they walk along, the disciples start picking heads of grain. They don't even stop, they just reach, like me walking past the chocolate chip station. The mustache has a mind of its OWN.

cards.question: The disciples are picking grain as they walk through the fields on the Sabbath. Who speaks up about it?
The Pharisees tell Jesus to look at what His disciples are doing in the grainfield. What's their problem with it?

answers.text: It is unlawful on the Sabbath

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question about David, who later became Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3): "Have you never read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and in need?" Asking the Pharisees if they've read the Scriptures is like asking ME if I've ever heard of an oven.

cards.question: Jesus says that during the high priesthood of Abiathar, a hungry David entered the house of God. What did David eat there?
The consecrated bread David ate in the house of God was lawful only for the priests.

cards.text: And David didn't keep that bread to himself. He gave some to his companions as well, which is more than I can say for me and a fresh cooling rack.

cards.question: After the story about David, Jesus declares who the Sabbath was made for. What does He say?

answers.text: The Sabbath was made for man
Man was made for the Sabbath
The Sabbath was made for priests

cards.question: Jesus keeps going. Because the Sabbath was made for man, He says someone is Lord even of the Sabbath. Who?

cards.text: Son of Man is how Jesus talks about Himself (Mark 2:10), so the Pharisees just tried to explain the Sabbath to its Lord. Friend, that's like explaining the oven to the guy who BUILT the bakery.
Once again Jesus goes into the synagogue. And a man with a withered hand is there.

cards.question: A man with a withered hand is in the synagogue, and some people there are watching Jesus. What are they watching for?

answers.text: If He will heal on the Sabbath
If He will read from the scroll
If He will teach the crowd

cards.question: The people in the synagogue are watching Jesus because they hope the man with the withered hand will get help.

cards.text: So they're watching in order to accuse Him, and Jesus says to the man with the withered hand, "Stand up among us." Right in the middle of everybody, which, for a guy who spent years in the back of a junk drawer, sounds TERRIFYING.

cards.question: With the man standing among them, Jesus asks which is lawful on the Sabbath. What is the first pair of choices He gives?

answers.text: To do good or to do evil

cards.question: Jesus asks if it's lawful on the Sabbath to do good or evil, to save life or destroy it. How do the people in the synagogue answer?

cards.text: They are silent, so quiet you could hear a sprinkle drop. Jesus looks around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart.

cards.question: Jesus says to the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man stretches it out, and his hand is ___.
After Jesus restores the man's hand, the Pharisees go out. Who do they start plotting with?
The Pharisees and the Herodians begin plotting how they might ___ Jesus.

cards.text: Jesus asked whether the Sabbath is for saving life or destroying it. He restores a man's hand, and they walk out plotting how to kill Him.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'One Sabbath...', 'As they walk along...', 'They don't even stop...', 'The mustache has a mind of its OWN.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks who the Sabbath was made for. The wrong answer 'Man was made for the Sabbath' says what man was made for, so it doesn't answer the question. It isn't the same kind of thing as the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The story card repeats Mark 3:1 almost word for word. It has none of Papa Dorin's voice, and it doesn't say this happens on a Sabbath, so the stop opens flat.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card says 'The people in the synagogue are watching Jesus.' Mark 3:2 only says 'they' were watching, which doesn't mean everyone in the synagogue. Card 2 handled this correctly with 'some people there.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question asks 'How do the people in the synagogue answer?' Mark 3:4 says Jesus asked 'them' and 'they were silent.' It never says the whole synagogue was asked or stayed silent.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The last story card only recaps Mark 3:4-6, which earlier cards already covered (Jesus's question, the hand restored, the plot to kill). It doesn't move the passage forward.

The card says 'Jesus asked whether the Sabbath is for saving life or destroying it.' Mark 3:4 has Jesus asking which is lawful on the Sabbath: to save life or to destroy it. That isn't asking what the Sabbath is for.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
